page: Amazon Web Services t3a.xlarge is a burstable general-purpose instance running on the Nitro hypervisor. It is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7571 processor clocked at 2.2 GHz, delivering 4 vCPUs provisioned across 2 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The configuration is equipped with 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory at 3 GHz, adhering to a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM proportion. Local instance storage is not included, requiring external block storage for operating system and application data, while baseline network throughput is rated at 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks show that the instance provides modest sustained compute and memory throughput. Geekbench testing yields scores of 692.0 in single-core and 1674.0 in multi-core tasks, while stress-ng multi-core testing registers 1181.97. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 23.87 GB/sec, with write bandwidth measuring 11.7 GB/sec. Despite lower relative compute throughput, the processor includes dedicated hardware support for cryptographic extensions such as AES and SHA_NI, which is reflected in a PassMark CPU encryption score of 3207.35.

The burstable CPU model makes t3a.xlarge cost-efficient for intermittent processing rather than continuous computational execution. The 16 GB memory footprint supports applications requiring substantial working memory without continuous CPU consumption. Suitable use cases include development environments, low-traffic web applications, staging infrastructure, build workers with low duty cycles, and microservices with variable resource demand.
description: Amazon Web Services t3a.xlarge is a burstable general-purpose virtual machine designed for workloads with variable compute requirements. Built on the Nitro hypervisor, it features 4 vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7571 processor running at 2.2 GHz, paired with 16.0 GB of DDR4 system memory. The instance does not include integrated local storage or hardware accelerators, depending instead on external EBS storage and a 1 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results indicate entry-tier compute and memory throughput, as seen in a Geekbench multi-core score of 1674.0 and uncached memory read bandwidth of 23.87 GB/sec, though integrated AES-NI delivers solid cryptographic throughput. The burstable credit architecture makes this configuration economically practical for memory-reliant, low-duty-cycle tasks such as staging environments, development application servers, internal tools, and light background processing services.
